item.title: Verona Park — Tue Sep 15, 4:30 PM
item.description:
Let's Walk!! JOIN US FOR A WALK
We will meet at the benches in front of the boathouse.
We will walk the loop around the park. The goal will be at least three miles, but there is plenty of opportunity to stop or continue to fit your personal goals.
We will be walking on a paved surface.
We walk at a medium speed.
Please plan to arrive 5 minutes **early** so that we can **start on time.**
Verona Park is 54.32 acres with a lake running through it. It is bordered by Lakeside and Bloomfield Avenues in the southern part of Verona. It is the fifth largest park in the Essex County system, making it a great place to walk.
Disclaimer: If you join us for a hike, please understand that you are responsible for your own preparedness and well-being and will hold no one else liable in case of injury or mishap. Event will be canceled in the event of extreme weather.
Source: Meetup: Let's Walk!!

item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.description: On Saturday, September 19, 2026, Start Out Fresh Intervention Advocates (S.O.F.I.A.) invites the community to affirm that “With Awareness There is Hope” at its 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence in beautiful Canterbury Park. Registration for the Walk begins at 9 AM, the program begins at 10 AM, and the event ends at Noon. S.O.F.I.A. is thrilled to welcome Dr. Zakiyyah Green as Grand Marshal for our 16th Annual Walk Against Domestic Violence. Dr. Green is a longtime volunteer and advocate with S.O.F.I.A. As Executive director of W.I.S.E. and CEO of Ministry Without Walls, LLC, Dr. Green blends biblical wisdom with practical life strategies. A Certified Domestic Violence Advocate, Dr. Green’s message inspires healing, restoration, and resilience, encouraging all to overcome adversity and live transformed lives. item.title: Valerie Huhn A Life Rebuilt in Fingerprints — Sat Sep 19, 4:00 PM — The BrassWorks Gallery
item.description: OPENING RECEPTION: Saturday, September 19, 4:00 – 6:00 PM EXHIBITION RUNS: September 19 – December 18, 2026 Montclair, NJ — The BrassWorks Gallery is honored and delighted to present a solo exhibition of work by artist Valerie Huhn. The exhibition, A Life Rebuilt in Fingerprints, brings together two decades of Huhn’s signature fingerprint-based practice – sculptures, murals, and mixed-media works built from thousands of the artist’s own fingerprints – in a body of work that transforms a tool of surveillance and identification into a language of individuality, memory, and belonging. For Huhn, this work is inseparable from her own history. As a teenager, she survived a car accident that left her with a traumatic brain injury – a neurological disability she still lives with today. item.title: Essential Oils Roller Workshop — Sat Sep 19, 5:00 PM — NJ
item.description:
In this hands-on workshop, participants will create their own custom essential oil roller blend for relaxation, grounding, focus, or energy. We will briefly explore the benefits of several essential oils and how aromatherapy can support daily wellness rituals. Participants will intuitively choose oils that resonate with them and blend them into a nourishing carrier oil. Each person will leave with a personalized roller bottle they can use as part of their self-care routine. This class is beginner-friendly that encourages creativity and intention. item.title: In-Person and Live Stream Service — Sun Sep 27, 10:00 AM — Sanctuary
item.description:
Sunday worship takes place at 10am in person at 176 Cooper Avenue in Montclair or livestreamed on our YouTube channel: Sunday Worship Livestream Union Congregational Church is located in Montclair, New Jersey, at 176 Cooper Avenue (nearest major cross streets are Grove Street and Valley Road). There is street parking on Cooper Avenue. We have a small parking lot for seniors and those with limited mobility reached through a driveway to the left of the church. There are two accessible spots and a ramp on the left side of the building. Additional parking is available on neighboring streets. Please note that Cooper Avenue runs one way on Sundays, so it is best to enter from Valley Road or Northview Avenue. Enter the church through the main Sanctuary doors under the tower or through the accessible entrance through the Assembly Room at the top of the ramp on the left side of the church. Join Us Here Click here for the Sunday Worship Bulletin
Source: Union Congregational Church

item.title: The Space for Music: Mr. Rose 'Dream House', with Era 'Of Love' — Sat Oct 3, 7:30 PM — the Space
item.description:
Saturday, October 3, at the Space, sliding scale donation $20 – $30
Doors open at 7:30pm Era ‘Of Love’ opening act beings at 8pm Mr. Rose starts at 8:30pm
Mr. Rose is back! These local favorites are at the Space to play their latest album in its entirety, ‘Dream House’. This will be a super special performance leading up to the release of the album at the end of this year, so come for the first listen!

John Sherman on vocals and accordion Fred Parcells on trombone Billy Loos on drums Dave Lockhart on upright bass

item.title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day — Sun Oct 4, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **TRAIL WORK (which was canceled Sept. 13th due to steady rain) will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)
Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required

item.title: Weekend Warrior Tennis (Sundays) — Sun Oct 4, 9:00 AM
item.description:
North Jersey Bowling, Volleyball, Tennis & More Join us for friendly and sociable free rallies and possibly some informal matches for training and fun. We are beginner to intermediate levels but all are welcome. We don’t allow formal instruction on our group-reserved courts, although giving some quick tips is OK so long as you’re not holding up others waiting to play.
⛑️ **Clinic Matches:** If we have to rotate people in then we may play some clinic-style matches where everyone rotates in evenly. There is no holding the court via wins so everyone has a chance to play regardless of skill level.
🕊️ **Early Bird Start:** If you want to meet earlier than 9 AM (like 8 or 8:30) then please let us know by the day before and we’ll see who can join you (usually I can do earlier).
**🎾 Equipment:** Please bring your own racquet and water, as we don’t provide those. I always have some balls for at least one court, but feel free to bring your own in case we need to branch out over more than one

item.description:

Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.

The village school in a remote farming community has been closed and converted into a detention center for political prisoners. item.title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day — Sun Nov 1, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)
Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). item.title: Men's Group Gathers at Pilgrim Diner — Sat Dec 12, 8:30 AM
item.description:
In the Spring of 2026, parishioner Ken Traficante began an informal once-a-month gathering of men at Holy Spirit Verona. Having chaired the Building and Grounds (B&G) Committee for many years, Ken wanted to recreate the fellowship that would happen on B&G Work Day events when parishioners volunteered time to clean up and repair items around the Church's campus. Ken scheduled a Saturday morning once a month at the Pilgrim Diner in Cedar Grove with a group of 6-8 guys during which they would share conversation and life experience with one another. This breakfast group will now meet on the second Saturday of each month from 8:30 to 10am (unless otherwise indicated on the website calendar). For more information, speak with Father Jerry or Ken Traficante.
Source: Church of the Holy Spirit Verona
